findings.title: Federated recovery codes are never marked as used
findings.body: After a successful validation, this code only checks whether the retrieved credential reports allCodesUsed(); it does not persist that the just-used code is now consumed. For a locally stored credential the local credential provider performs that consumption during isValid(), but for a federated user validation is delegated to the user-storage validator and that local side effect does not happen. The storage implementation added in this PR likewise only checks for a matching raw code and its getCredentials() recreates every code as unused. Consequently the same federated recovery code can be replayed indefinitely, getNextRecoveryAuthnCode() keeps prompting for the first code, and the exhaustion check/regeneration required action at lines 85-92 never triggers.

findings.title: Login bean throws NoSuchElementException when federated credential cannot be retrieved
findings.body: The constructor unconditionally calls credentialModelOpt.get() (and then getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get() on line 21). RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential() now prefers getFederatedCredentialsStream(), which is a different provider capability from the isConfiguredFor() check that allowed the user into this flow: a federated validator can report the user as configured and validate codes without exposing a readable credential model, in which case both the federated and local lookups are empty. The login form then fails with NoSuchElementException/500 instead of rendering the recovery-code challenge.

findings.title: getCredentials() loses the stored recovery credential's identity, label and used state
findings.body: updateCredential() stores a CredentialModel with a generated id at line 195, but getCredentials() discards that stored model and fabricates a new RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel via createFromValues(rawCodes, createdDate, userLabel) without copying the stored id, and with every code re-created as unused (the stored userLabel is also never set in updateCredential(), so it is always null). Production code depends on this model both for the next-code number (LoginBean) and for removeStoredCredentialById(model.getId()) when codes are exhausted (RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator), so neither flow can address or track the actual federated credential correctly.

findings.title: Federated recovery credential cannot be disabled or deleted
findings.body: This PR adds recovery codes to supportsCredentialType(), updateCredential(), isConfiguredFor() and isValid(), but disableCredentialType() still only handles OTP types and getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() still only returns OTP. Federated credential removal (used by admin/account deletion and by RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator when all codes are used via removeStoredCredentialById) is delegated to disableCredentialType(), so a federated recovery credential silently survives deletion attempts and remains valid afterwards.

findings.title: No test covers the fallback to local storage for federated users
findings.body: The new test only covers a federated provider that supports recovery codes, asserting the codes land in user storage and not in the DB. The other half of the feature title/branch in CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential() - updateCredential() returning false (federated provider does not support the type, read-only storage, or imported user) and the credential then being created in the local DB and still usable for login - is never exercised for a federated user, so a regression in the local fallback for federated users would not be caught.
